theme: A blight sweeps a one-variety crop

then.title: Ireland’s Great Famine begins
then.hook: A fungus rots Ireland’s potatoes, and a country living on one crop starves.
then.text: In 1845 a blight caused by Phytophthora infestans began rotting Ireland’s potatoes, the main food of the rural poor, who relied heavily on a single variety, the Lumper. About one million people died and over a million emigrated.

now.title: A banana fungus reaches Latin America
now.hook: In August 2019 Colombia declared a national emergency after a soil fungus reached its banana farms.
now.text: Tropical Race 4, a strain of Panama disease, was confirmed on Colombian banana farms in 2019. About 99% of exported bananas are a single clone, the Cavendish, which has no resistance to it.

followed: Ireland’s population fell by about a fifth within a decade. In 1861 Anton de Bary showed that a microbe caused the blight, helping found the science of plant disease.

next.title: A pathogen hits a global staple
next.text: Around 2193, a new pathogen could sweep through a staple grown worldwide from a handful of genetic lines, forcing a rushed switch to new varieties.
next.watch: A few varieties covering most of a crop, fungal strains spreading in soil and seed, and warmer weather helping pathogens reach new regions.

breaks: In Ireland, poverty, land tenure and government policy turned a crop failure into mass death; losing the Cavendish would raise prices and hurt growers, not starve nations.
